summary: Periodic p99 latency oscillations caused by continuous batcher queue-depth feedback loop
description:
Issue summary:
VectorMetrics reported recurring p95/p99 latency spikes in production that occur in 3–7 minute windows roughly every 15 minutes. Spikes correlate with increased queue depth in the continuous batcher leading to delayed flushes and bursty GPU utilization.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference latency p99 increases from ~180ms to 1.6–2.4s during each spike window.
- Errors: elevated 504s observed during two windows on 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-11 (customer: dedicated pool).
- Business impact: degraded UX for interactive product; customer reports reduced engagement during windows.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster: pool-id vm-dedicated-us-east-7
- Region: us-east-1
- Models: open/redwood-vicuna-7b for short-chat flows; quantized/redwood-gptq-3b for embeddings fallbacks

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Run a steady multi-connection short-stream workload: 80 concurrent connections from a single tenant, steady 12 qps aggregate, prompt length 8–24 tokens, average response length 30–60 tokens.
2) Observe continuous-batcher queue depth metric and batch flush latency via /metrics/batcher.* and per-tenant trace.
3) Wait 10–20 minutes to capture oscillation window.

Observed metrics & logs:
- batcher.queue_depth (tenant vm-dedicated-us-east-7) shows sawtooth growth from 0→~320 over 3–5 minutes, then abrupt drain.
- batcher.flush_latency_p95 spikes to 900–1,800ms in the same windows.
- serving-runtime.gpu_utilization shows burst to 95% during drains and idle at ~25% between bursts.
- API gateway shows increased request queueing and occasional 504s: logs show upstream timeout after 30s in two traces.
- No corresponding OOMs, no GPU driver errors.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Increased continuous-batcher.flush_threshold to 200 for the affected pool (rolled 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC) which reduced spike magnitude by ~40% and eliminated 504s for a follow-up 6-hour window.

Notes:
- Behavior appears to be a feedback loop: higher queue depth delays flush; delayed flushes cause longer per-batch processing which increases queueing, exacerbating delay until a large batch drains and GPU is saturated.
- This is distinct from idle-linger growth; it looks like scheduler/backpressure settings plus tenant-level request burst patterns are creating resonance.
comments: 2026-03-11 09:12 Priya Desai (Support): Customer opened with p99 spikes; attached metrics and sample request IDs. Requested immediate triage.
2026-03-11 10:05 Ethan Walker (SRE): Confirmed recurring spikes on our cluster graphs. No driver OOMs. Assigned to continuous-batcher on-call.

2026-03-11 12:30 Maria Chen (Batching Eng): Hypothesis: queue_depth-based flush policy interacts poorly with concurrent short streams. Proposing to test lowering max_batch_wait and adding a soft cap on queue depth per-tenant.
2026-03-12 03:42 Ethan Walker (SRE): Temporarily raised flush_threshold to 200 for vm-dedicated-us-east-7 as a mitigation; customer reports reduced errors. Monitoring.

2026-03-13 08:25 VectorMetrics (Customer): Noticed improvement after mitigation but still seeing small p99 blips. Asking for ETA on permanent fix and whether changes affect latency for larger requests.
investigation_notes: Collected tenant-level traces for affected requests (trace IDs attached in support system).
Profiling shows batch processing time grows nonlinearly once batch size > 128 for the quantized model due to KV cache backend contention.
Scheduler logs show adaptive backpressure was toggling between 'aggressive' and 'conservative' modes every few minutes, matching oscillation cadence.
Found correlation between a background job (tenant-side periodic health pings) and the initial queue growth; these pings are bursty and align with spike start times.
Related PRs touch flush heuristics: serving-runtime PR #3421 and batcher PR #128 — both referenced for potential fixes.
action_items: (SRE) Keep mitigation in place and extend monitoring window to 72 hours to validate stability.
(Batching Eng) Run controlled repro using tenant workload simulator with periodic small bursts and measure queue-depth thresholds (owner: Maria Chen, ETA 2026-03-17).
(Batching Eng) Prototype soft queue cap per-tenant that triggers earlier partial flushes when KV contention is detected (owner: Maria Chen, ETA prototype 2026-03-20).
(Platform) Add tenant-level metric export for burst-pattern detection to alert before oscillations (owner: Platform Observability, ETA 2026-03-24).
(Support) Coordinate with VectorMetrics about controlled window for testing and notify about possible small regression for long-sequence cold-starts.
resolution: Mitigation: flush_threshold increased to 200 for the affected dedicated pool which reduced spike amplitude and eliminated timeouts in the short-term. Permanent fix pending: implement soft per-tenant queue cap and adjust adaptive backpressure to avoid mode flapping. Customer notified and monitoring extended.
workaround: Increase continuous-batcher.flush_threshold or reduce per-tenant concurrency; schedule tenant-side burst smoothing. Workaround applied for this customer.
follow_up: Postmortem to be created if spikes recur after mitigation window expires (owner: Ethan Walker).
If prototype soft-cap reduces p99 in test, schedule rollout in canary and then to all dedicated pools with rollback plan.
